generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to work you are already doing or about to do. Practice and work-based learning, a placement, laboratory or studio work, field work, a simulation or a project, is where your subject meets real settings and real decisions. The students who treat each experience as something to aim for, act on and learn from are the ones whose skills and confidence grow fastest. Treat what follows as being about your own placements and projects, not about work experience in the abstract.

The same cycle runs through professional life. You are given real work, you act in a real setting, and you are expected to show what you gained from it. Learning to aim for value, take initiative and evidence what you learned is a habit you keep long after you graduate.
